leads.title: Penal Code of 1791 and Penal Code of 1810
leads.documents: Decriminalisation of same-sex sexual activity in private in France, retained in 1810 Code and followed in French colonies; foundational legal status applicable to Wallis and Futuna as French territory.
leads.detail: No URL in excerpt; citation detail visible: 'Penal Code of 1791 made no mention of same-sex relations in private' retained in 'Penal Code of 1810'

leads.title: French Penal Code Article 225-1 as amended by Law of 18 November 2016
leads.documents: Discrimination protections on grounds of sexual orientation and gender identity in employment, housing, services; core anti-discrimination machinery for trans visitors.
leads.detail: No URL in excerpt; citation detail visible: 'On 18 November 2016, a new law amended article 225-1 of the French Penal Code to replace sexual identity with gender identity'; prior steps 1985 sexual orientation, July 2012 sexual identity

leads.title: Code du travail (Labour Code) Chapter 2
leads.documents: Prohibits exclusion from recruitment, sanction, dismissal or discriminatory measure on account of sexual orientation, gender identity, among other grounds.
leads.detail: No URL in excerpt; citation detail visible: quoted text 'No person may be excluded from a recruitment process...' listing 'sexual orientation, gender identity'

leads.title: Law of 18 November 2016 on legal gender change - Journal Officiel / Constitutional Council decision of 17 November
leads.documents: Allows transgender people to legally change gender without surgery or sterilisation, via court order from 1 January 2017; no psychiatrist certificates or proof of surgery required, first-name change via registry office.
leads.detail: No URL in excerpt; citation detail visible: 'approved by French Senate 6 Nov 2015', 'National Assembly 24 May 2016', '12 July 2016', '12 Oct', 'Constitutional Council ruled bill constitutional 17 Nov', 'signed 18 Nov 2016, published in Journal Officiel next day, took effect 1 Jan 2017'

leads.title: B. vs France - European Court of Human Rights (1992)
leads.documents: Court ruling that ended decades-long French legislative ban on legal gender change even after medical/surgical transition; basis for later gender-recognition law.
leads.detail: No URL in excerpt; citation detail visible: '1992 case, B. vs France at the European Court of Human Rights changed this'

leads.title: Law No. 2013-404 opening marriage to same-sex couples - Constitutional Council ruling 17 May 2013, Journal Officiel 19 May 2013
leads.documents: Legalises same-sex marriage and joint adoption throughout France including overseas departments and territories including Wallis and Futuna; first ceremony 29 May Montpellier.
leads.detail: No URL in excerpt; citation detail visible: 'Senate approved 12 April', 'National Assembly 23 April', 'Council ruled law constitutional 17 May 2013', 'signed 18 May 2013, published next day in Journal Officiel'

leads.title: Law of 31 December 2004 amending Law on Freedom of the Press of 29 July 1881 (Title 3, Articles 20 and 21) + Haute autorite de lutte contre les discriminations et pour l'egalite
leads.documents: Criminalises homophobic/sexist/racist comments, injury, defamation, incitement to hatred/violence/discrimination based on gender, sexual orientation or disability; increased penalties for bias-motivated assault/murder; creates equality enforcement body.
leads.detail: No URL in excerpt; citation detail visible: 'National Assembly approved amendment 31 Dec 2004', 'maximum penalty EUR45,000 fine and/or 12 months imprisonment', 'Title 3 and articles 20 and 21 of law amended Law on Freedom of Press of 29 July 1881'

leads.title: ILGA-Europe report published 2022 on France
leads.documents: Institutional human-rights report documenting significant issues with gender-affirming healthcare provision in France: lack of self-determination, extended waiting times, inequitable access by location; recommends informed consent model.
leads.detail: No URL in excerpt; citation detail visible: 'A report published in 2022 by ILGA-Europe found significant issues with the provision of gender affirming healthcare in France'

leads.title: Law banning conversion therapy - Senate 7 Dec 2020, National Assembly 25 Jan 2022, published 1 Feb 2022
leads.documents: Legally bans conversion therapy with punishments of two years imprisonment and/or 30,000 euro fine; documents state protection against forced conversion practices.
leads.detail: No URL in excerpt; citation detail visible: 'bill to legally ban conversion therapy passed Senate 7 Dec 2020', 'concurred by National Assembly 25 Jan 2022 and officially published 1 Feb 2022'; proposal by MP Laurence Vanceunebrock-Mialon summer 2019

leads.title: DILCRAH - French Interministerial Delegation for the Fight Against Racism, Anti-Semitism, and Anti-LGBT Hatred
leads.documents: Government rights machinery responsible for anti-LGBT hatred policy; 2022 controversy over president of scientific committee membership in The Little Mermaid Observatory noted as context on institutional stance.
